known.title: Decision 2 drops the root context-tree row for docs/AGENTS.md while docs/AGENTS.md stays, so tree/guard fails and the full gate of a1 cannot pass
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 2 (line 25); Goal (line 5); Steps, row 1 remove_records (line 39); Acceptance, a1 (line 46)
known.summary: Decision 2 drops the context-tree row for docs/AGENTS.md from the root AGENTS.md, because Claude Code and Codex load a nested AGENTS.md without a row. The runtimes do load nested nodes, but the Goal and decision 2 keep docs/AGENTS.md, and the root AGENTS.md at repo_ref (Context tree, line 49) says the table must name every AGENTS.md below the root and that scripts/tree/guard.mjs enforces it. scripts/tree/guard.mjs lines 77-83 collect the backticked AGENTS.md paths from table lines only and fail with 'docs/AGENTS.md - node not routed from the root AGENTS.md table' for a nested node without a row. The repo-wide guards section of scripts/ci.mjs (lines 290-292) runs tree/guard, so step 1 makes a1 (bun scripts/ci.mjs) fail; the row must stay and be updated, not dropped.

known.title: Step 2 removes the no-bespoke-gates gate step but its Files cell omits scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs, so the assertion that the repo lane runs the guard once stays and the CI targeting check fails
known.locator: Steps, row 2 remove_guard (line 40); Research, Decisions, decision 3 (line 26); Research, Facts (line 16)
known.summary: Decision 3 removes the gate step and the ci-plugin-targeting assertion, and Facts names scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs, but the Files cell of step 2 (the only step that implements decision 3) no longer lists that file, and plan-contract.md at repo_ref (Steps, acceptance, and effects, lines 70-71) makes Files the scope of a step. At repo_ref, scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs line 679 asserts countToolInvocation(repoWide.calls, 'bun', ['scripts/plans/no-bespoke-gates.mjs']) equals 1; it runs in --unit mode (unitOnly gating starts at line 1957), and scripts/ci.mjs lines 312-323 run that file with --unit in the gate. Once step 2 deletes the gate step at scripts/ci.mjs lines 293-295, the count is 0, the CI targeting contract fails, and the step-2 Done when (CI targeting checks pass) and a1 cannot be met inside the step's scope.

known.title: Decision 5 writes the review diffs to a literal .git/docks-review/ path, against the repository rule to use the git rev-parse --git-path docks-review directory and to keep scratch paths out of durable records
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 5 (line 28); Goal, Yolo line (line 7)
known.summary: Decision 5 sends the review diffs to `.git/docks-review/`. The root AGENTS.md at repo_ref (Tool-agnostic rules, line 105) says review bundles belong in the docks-review directory that `git rev-parse --git-path docks-review` resolves, and that in a linked worktree `.git` is a file, so a literal `.git/...` path fails with ENOTDIR. This is a yolo plan (line 7), and plan-contract.md at repo_ref (Yolo runs, Linked branch timing, lines 604-615) does all later work in a linked worktree when the checkout is dirty; plan-contract.md line 302 puts scratch at `git rev-parse --git-path docks-review` and line 309 says to keep scratch and machine paths out of durable records such as the plan body. The git-worktree documentation (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree, DETAILS) confirms that a linked worktree has a .git file and says to use git rev-parse --git-path instead of a direct path. The decision breaks the repository rule and fails in a linked worktree.

known.title: The two-commit split of step 2 leaves a red first commit and no commit that reverts alone, so the claim that each commit stays green and either one can be reverted alone is false
known.locator: Research, Engineering standards, Commits (line 33); Steps, row 2 remove_guard (line 40)
known.summary: Engineering standards split step 2 into a first commit that deletes the guard script, its unit test, and its fixtures, and a second commit with the registry row, the gate step, and the text edits, and claim that each commit stays green and either one reverts alone. At repo_ref the first commit is red: scripts/ci.mjs lines 293-295 still run `bun scripts/plans/no-bespoke-gates.mjs` (bun 1.4.4, the packageManager pin, exits 1 with 'Module not found' for a missing script); scripts/tests/author-tooling.mjs line 220 fails on the scripts/AGENTS.md row (line 62) for a missing script; scripts/tests/test-contracts.mjs line 570 (discovered vs registered) and line 595 (owner suite does not exist) fail on the row unit-no-bespoke-gates in scripts/config/test-contracts.json. A revert of either commit alone gives the same broken mix: reverting the second restores the gate step and rows for a deleted guard, and reverting the first restores a guard and a unit test without their rows (author-tooling.mjs line 217, test-contracts.mjs lines 153-167 and 570). The commit-discipline skill that the plan names (plugins/docks/skills/engineering/commit-discipline/SKILL.md lines 29-32) requires every commit to leave the tree green and makes changes that cannot be split into green commits one commit. So the planned rollback cannot happen, and the history holds a red commit that breaks git bisect and git revert.
